findings.title: Duplicate receipt output is order-dependent despite byte-stability contract
findings.what: The duplicate check at src/lib/semantic-intent.ts:393-396 defines an identical verdict using only contentSha256, intentClass, and canonicalTaskClass. If two rows share those fields and evidenceRef but have different confidence or classifiedAt values, the first row is retained and the second is discarded. Reversing artifact or row order therefore changes rows[].confidence, rows[].classifiedAt, and potentially summary.asOf, contradicting the deterministic byte-stability contract. The order-stability test at src/lib/semantic-intent.test.ts:108-112 uses two different evidenceRef values, so it cannot detect this duplicate-order case.
findings.fix: Make duplicate resolution deterministic: either require every persisted row field, including confidence and classifiedAt, to match before treating a re-emission as identical, or select a documented winner using a total ordering. Add a reversed-order duplicate regression test.
findings.acceptance: Create two receipts with the same evidenceRef, hash, intent class, and canonical scope but different confidence and classifiedAt. Assert that ingestSemanticIntent for both input orders produces byte-identical JSON and the same asOf; also retain coverage that genuinely conflicting classifications degrade to unknown.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that src/lib/semantic-intent.ts:393-396 excludes confidence and classifiedAt while src/lib/semantic-intent.ts:400-406 keeps the first row for sameVerdict duplicates. The only byte-stability test, src/lib/semantic-intent.test.ts:108-112, uses distinct references, and the duplicate test at lines 169-175 uses fully identical rows, so neither refutes the order-dependent case.
